      YAML.

      `final_output` and `relationship_output`, while keeping `workflow_output`
      as the pre-relationship debug view.
- [ ] Match children to parents only when the parent and child share the same
      non-empty present `match_attrs` key set and all present values match.
- [ ] Implement Arcadia-compatible match comparison: unwrap extracted-field
      wrappers, ignore blank/missing values, compare strings case-insensitively,
      compare numeric ints/floats by value, require the same non-empty present
      match-key set on parent and child, and do not date-normalize strings.
- [ ] Preserve unmatched children in `unmatched_child_group` when configured.
- [ ] Return clear diagnostics for invalid relationship metadata, missing parent
      or child groups, and child records that match multiple parents.
- [ ] Support chained relationships so one nested child list can itself be the
      parent of another nested list.
- [ ] Keep `Document.load_custom_outputs()` on the helper instead of maintaining
      a second parser.
- [ ] Do not move prompt authoring, compile/deploy/run ergonomics, scoring,
      Arcadia-specific dedupe, Arcadia requiredness, passthrough, reconcile, QA,
      or final rendering policy into the SDK as part of this change.

## 4. Step Kind Support

- [ ] Keep SDK-supported custom step kinds as `instruct`, `keys`, and
      `summary`.
- [ ] Treat `instruct` as singular-object output.
- [ ] Treat `keys` and `summary` as repeated-record output.
- [ ] Keep `keys` and `summary` distinct backend step-family names while giving
      both repeated-record readback semantics.
- [ ] Ensure prepared workflow metadata exposes each route's effective output
      kind as a derived lookup so readback can detect repeated direct groups
      without final group name checks.
- [ ] Ensure `leaf_fields.is_repeated` does not cause direct `keys` or
      `summary` routes to be treated as singular during readback.
- [ ] Validate unsupported kind values with a clear error.
- [ ] Do not infer repeated groups from names such as `meters`, `charges`,
      `doctors`, or `line_items`.

Simplify electron bootstrap derived state (#18)

* feat(electron): simplify bootstrap to derived state (LaunchSource V2)

Implements OpenSpec change `simplify-electron-bootstrap-derived-state`.
Replaces stored startup decisions (`mode.json`, `isFirstRun`,
`decideStartupAction`) with derived-on-launch capability probes plus an
explicit `DASHBOARD_STARTER` env var stamped on every server spawn.

New capabilities
- electron-launch-source: discriminated `LaunchSource` resolver across
  attach / devMonorepo / piExtension / npmGlobal / extracted, with
  `DASHBOARD_PREFER_SOURCE` override.
- electron-bundle-extract: version-marker-driven extraction of
  `~/.pi-dashboard/`, config migration to `~/.pi/dashboard/migrate/<ts>/`,
  and the `node|node-pending|node-old` survive-extract whitelist.
- dashboard-starter-identity: `DASHBOARD_STARTER` env contract,
  `/api/health.starter` + `/api/health.pid` exposure, lifecycle ownership
  rule "only the starter, with pid match, may stop on quit".
- installable-list: `~/.pi/dashboard/installable.json` schema +
  server-side reconcile in `bootstrap-install-from-list.ts` (no-op when
  file absent).

Removed
- first-run-wizard capability: `mode.json`, `isFirstRun`,
  `decideStartupAction`, `runPowerUserManagedInstall` deletions deferred
  to a follow-up change once `LAUNCH_SOURCE_V2=false` legacy path is
  retired.
- NSIS installer + portable .exe: ZIP is now the sole Windows
  distribution (cross-platform reproducible from Docker).

Phase C bring-up fixes (Windows ZIP)
- launch-source.ts: extract from `<resourcesPath>/server`, not bare
  `resourcesPath` (top-level contains app.asar, recursive cpSync ENOTDIRs
  on opendir).
- launch-source.ts: extraction error log now includes
  code/syscall/path/message so failing entry is identifiable.
- docker-make.sh: replace every workspace symlink under
  `node_modules/@blackbelt-technology/*`, not a hardcoded subset
  (previously missed `dashboard-plugin-runtime`, dangling symlink tripped
  ENOTDIR on Windows first-launch cpSync).
- build-windows-zip.sh: anonymous Docker volume on
  `/build/packages/electron/out` to dodge Docker Desktop FUSE/VirtioFS
  EACCES on read-after-write; `--platform linux/amd64` pinned on build
  and run; `--name` + `docker cp` artifact extraction.

Supersedes
- electron-startup-splash (archived)
- electron-wizard-smart-detection (archived)

* test(electron): real-fs smoke for LaunchSource V2 + fix bootstrap regressions

Adds a tiered real-fs smoke test for the `extracted` source path that
catches the class of bugs unit tests can't see (pure mocks miss
real-fs/npm/spawn behavior). Fixes three production regressions
the smoke test surfaced.

New test file
- packages/electron/src/lib/__tests__/launch-source.smoke.test.ts
  - Tier A (always when bundle present, ~2s): real `extractBundle` over
    the host's `resources/server/`; pins layout + cliPath presence + no
    absolute symlinks.
  - Tier B (when offline cache + bundled node also present, ~30s):
    `selectLaunchSource({ preferOverride: "extracted" })` end-to-end;
    pins pi-coding-agent install, cliPath survival, jiti resolution.
  - Tier C (when host node-pty prebuild matches, ~10s): real `node
    --import <jiti> <cliPath>` spawn; pins /api/health = starter:Electron.
  - Skips cleanly with explicit reasons when prerequisites absent;
    fresh-clone friendly.

Production fixes uncovered by the smoke test

1. cpSync rewrites relative symlinks as absolute paths (Node quirk)
   - Repro: `fs.cpSync(src, dst, { recursive: true, dereference: false })`
     on a relative symlink writes an absolute path pointing at the build
     host's source tree. Users see a broken cliPath after extraction.
   - Fix: bundle-server.mjs materializes every workspace symlink under
     `@blackbelt-technology/*` before forge packs the bundle. Mirrors
     what docker-make.sh already does (Linux/Windows build paths) but
     covers native-macOS builds (build-installer.sh path) too.

2. npm install --prefix reconciles node_modules and prunes the bundle
   - Repro: with the bundle's package.json declaring no deps,
     `npm install --prefix <managedDir> @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent` wipes
     every existing node_modules/@blackbelt-technology/* AND every server
     runtime dep (fastify, node-pty, ws, ...). Stripping `workspaces` and
     deleting package-lock didn't help; the reconciliation rules vary by
     npm version.
   - Fix: swap-aside in resolveExtracted. Move
     <managedDir>/node_modules → <managedDir>/.bundle-node-modules,
     run installStandalone (npm builds a fresh tree containing only
     pi+tsx+openspec deps), then cpSync the stash back over node_modules.
     Bundle wins on conflicts (it's the version the server was tested
     against. Mostly additive merge because pi's namespace
     (@mariozechner/*) doesn't overlap with bundle deps.

3. installStandalone was missing from V2 (re-affirmed)
   - Smoke test pins that runtime baseline install runs after
     extractBundle, before any spawn would resolve jiti.

OpenSpec proposal updates
- design.md: new Bundle source path / Workspace symlink materialization
  / Runtime baseline install (jiti chicken-and-egg) / Swap-aside pattern
  sections.
- tasks.md: §13 Phase C bring-up tasks 13.1–13.8 (impl) + 13.9 (QA).

Compatibility
- No API/wire changes.
- managedDir layout: now contains a transient
  during the swap-aside; cleaned up on the same tick.
- Migration: none. Phase C hasn't shipped to users yet.
- Rollback: revert this commit + the parent feat commit.
EOF
)

* test(electron): clean-Ubuntu Docker test for V2 LaunchSource bootstrap

Modernizes packages/electron/scripts/test-electron-install{,-inner}.sh
to drive the Phase C V2 path on clean Ubuntu 22.04 instead of the
legacy tsx-wizard flow.

Stages (23 assertions, ~3 min cold):
  1. Verify bundled resource layout (Node, npm, server bundle, cliPath,
     offline cacache, node-pty linux-x64 prebuild, no abs symlinks).
  2. extractBundle (cp -a) into ~/.pi-dashboard/.
  3. Strip workspaces field from package.json + delete bundle's lockfile.
  4. Swap-aside node_modules → .bundle-node-modules.
  5. npm install --prefix --cache from offline cacache (pi+tsx+openspec
     pinned via offline-packages/manifest.json).
  6. Merge .bundle-node-modules back; verify cliPath + jiti both present.
  7. Spawn node --import <jiti-register> <cliPath>.
  8. curl /api/health within 120s; assert starter==Electron.

What this catches that the host smoke can't:
  - Linux glibc-linked node-pty native module.
  - clean-Ubuntu npm reconciliation (vs host npm version).
  - non-root user permissions.
  - bundled Node v22.18.0 (production pin) instead of host's Node.

Drops legacy assertions:
  - tsx-wizard flow / mode.json write (V2 deletes mode.json).
  - Per-package CJS/ESM checks (no longer relevant to V2 path).
  - Direct pi spawn tests (covered by other tests).

OpenSpec tasks 13.10–13.13 added documenting the test artifacts and
the production fixes they pin (smoke + Docker variants).

* test(qa): Windows VM bootstrap test for V2 LaunchSource ZIP

Adds qa/tests/07-electron-bootstrap-v2.ps1 invoked by
qa/tests/run-all.ps1 inside a Packer-built Windows VM. Drives the
production PI-Dashboard-win32-x64.zip end-to-end:

  1. Verify resources layout (server bundle, cliPath, offline cacache,
     bundled node.exe).
  2. Extract ZIP to C:\PI-Dashboard-test\.
  3. Launch pi-dashboard.exe.
  4. Poll /api/health (default port 8000) up to 180s.
  5. Assert starter==Electron, version present.
  6. Verify ~\.pi-dashboard\.version, @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent
     installation, and cliPath survival post-install (the swap-aside
     pattern from launch-source.ts).
  7. Clean up: stop process, remove extract dir.

Skips with a clear message when the ZIP artifact is absent so the
test suite still passes on VMs without a fresh build.

qa/scripts/run-test.sh: optional ZIP upload step. Looks for
packages/electron/out/make/zip/x64/PI-Dashboard-win32-x64.zip by
default, scp's to C:\qa-artifacts\ before running tests. Override
location via QA_ELECTRON_ZIP env var.

qa/README.md updated with the new test description and ZIP upload
instructions.

OpenSpec task 13.14 added documenting the qa artifact and what it
catches that Linux Docker can't see (Windows path semantics: drive
letters, junction points, \ vs /).

* chore(build): purge stale NSIS references from Docker build scripts

NSIS was removed earlier (forge.config.ts maker entry + package.json
devDep, per openspec change simplify-electron-bootstrap-derived-state),
but the build scripts still advertised it in help text, banners, and
inline comments. The Docker entrypoint also accepted ZIP_ONLY=1 from
its callers but ignored the flag.

build-installer.sh:
  - Header comment: Windows artifacts now described as
    .zip + portable .exe (not '.exe (NSIS)').
  - --help: dropped (NSIS) parenthetical from --windows. --windows-zip
    described as 'no portable' (was 'no NSIS, no portable').
  - Plan-banner line: split into two states reflecting whether
    --windows-zip is in effect.
  - Docker build comment: rationale rewritten without mentioning
    NSIS/makensis (the real reason is x64 native module ABI).

docker-make.sh:
  - Forge package step comment: explains we use forge for packaging
    only and produce ZIP via 'zip' + optional portable via
    electron-builder. Drops 'NSIS can't run on Linux' framing.
  - Portable-exe step now honors ZIP_ONLY=1: skips the
    electron-builder invocation and emits a single skip line.
    Previously the env var was passed but ignored, so --windows and
    --windows-zip produced identical output.

No production code paths touched; ZIP / portable artifacts produced
when ZIP_ONLY=0 are byte-identical to before.

* openspec: add automate-windows-remote-qa change

Adds proposal, design, specs, and tasks for a remote-Windows QA harness
under qa/remote/. Drives a real Windows host on the LAN over OpenSSH;
covers three artifact modes (ZIP, portable.exe, npm-global); reuses the
existing qa/tests/*.ps1 suite; idempotent clean-state via process kill,
port reclaim, AppData removal, portable extract-dir glob, and PID/log
cleanup. Purely additive — no production code changes.

4/4 artifacts complete; openspec validate --strict passes.

* fix(build-windows): skip electron-builder code-signing pass

No Windows certificate is configured, but electron-builder's default
CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=true causes it to attempt signing anyway,

* build(electron): pin appdmg + fail fast on incompatible Node versions

When building the macOS DMG locally on Node 25, the Electron build failed
deep inside electron-forge with 'Cannot find module appdmg'. Two contributing
gaps:

  1. `appdmg` is an *optional* transitive dep of `electron-installer-dmg`
     (used by `@electron-forge/maker-dmg`). On certain npm runs it gets
     skipped silently, leaving DMG building broken with no upfront signal.

  2. `appdmg` itself depends on `macos-alias`, a native module that does
     not compile on Node 25 (V8 internal API changes). Today this surfaces
     only when the user runs `npm run electron:build` — too late and too
     opaque.

Fixes:

  - Add `appdmg` to root `optionalDependencies` so npm always attempts
    the install rather than skipping it as a deep transitive optional.
  - Add root `engines.node` (`>=22.12.0 <25`) — `<25` excludes the
    macos-alias-incompatible Node 25 line. Documented prerequisite in
    docs/faq.md is already "Node.js 22.12+", so this codifies it.
  - Add `.npmrc` with `engine-strict=true` so a fresh `npm install` on
    Node 25 fails fast with EBADENGINE rather than silently skipping
    optional `appdmg` and erroring at `electron-forge make` time.

Verified:

  - Node 22.22.2: `npm install` succeeds, `node_modules/appdmg/` present.
  - Node 25.8.1: `npm install --dry-run` errors with `EBADENGINE` — fail fast.

Discovered while running the local Intel macOS DMG build for the
`doctor-rich-output` change. Build now completes cleanly to
`packages/electron/out/make/PI-Dashboard-darwin-x64-0.4.6.dmg` (156 MB).

Followups (not in this commit):

  - Add the engines/Node guidance to docs/faq.md / electron-build-methods.md
    so future contributors hit the explicit error message before reaching
    for an unfamiliar build script.
  - Track Node 26+ compatibility for `macos-alias`; widen the engines range

**Critical: cache the token in memory** after reading from SecureStorage on login — this keeps the request interceptor synchronous (reads from memory, not async SecureStorage). On login: `await SecureStorage.set()` + update memory cache. On request: read from memory cache (synchronous). On logout: clear both.

- [ ] Task 9: Migrate AuthContext, api.ts, SessionTimeoutWarning
  **Action:** Replace all `localStorage.getItem('fabt_access_token')` and related calls with `tokenStorage`. Ensure async nature of SecureStorage is handled (the calls are now `await`).

### Phase 3 — Push Notifications

- [ ] Task 10: Backend — Flyway migration for device_token table
  **File:** `V31__create_device_token.sql`
  **Action:** `device_token` table: id (UUID), user_id (UUID FK), token (VARCHAR 500), platform (VARCHAR 10), created_at (TIMESTAMPTZ). Unique constraint on (user_id, token).

- [ ] Task 11: Backend — DeviceTokenRepository and registration endpoint
  **Files:** `DeviceTokenRepository.java`, `DeviceController.java`
  **Action:** `POST /api/v1/devices` (register token), `DELETE /api/v1/devices/{token}` (unregister). Upsert on register. Authenticated endpoint.

- [ ] Task 12: Backend — Push notification sender (direct HTTP, no Firebase SDK)
  **File:** `PushNotificationSender.java` (new)
  **Action:** Use direct FCM HTTP v1 API calls (no `firebase-admin` SDK dependency — keeps the backend cloud-provider-agnostic). Authenticate via Google service account JWT (short-lived OAuth2 token). Send method accepts user ID + payload, looks up device tokens, sends via `https://fcm.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/messages:send`. Auto-deregisters invalid tokens on 404/410 response. Requires: `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` env var pointing to service account JSON. No new Maven dependencies — uses existing `java.net.http.HttpClient`.

- [ ] Task 13: Backend — Integrate push into NotificationService
  **File:** `NotificationService.java`
  **Action:** After SSE broadcast, call `PushNotificationSender.send()` for the same event. Dual delivery: SSE for foreground web users, FCM for backgrounded native users. Push is fire-and-forget (don't block SSE delivery on push failure).

- [ ] Task 14: Frontend — Push notification registration on native
  **File:** `frontend/src/hooks/usePushNotifications.ts` (new)
  **Action:** On native platform after login: request permission, get FCM token via `@capacitor/push-notifications`, register with `POST /api/v1/devices`. Handle token refresh. Handle foreground notification display.

- [ ] Task 15: Backend integration tests for push
  **Action:** Test device registration, unregistration, duplicate handling. Mock FCM sender for unit tests.

### Phase 4 — Biometric Auth

- [ ] Task 16: Install biometric plugin
  **Action:** `npm install @capawesome-team/capacitor-biometrics`

- [ ] Task 17: Implement biometric unlock flow
  **File:** `frontend/src/hooks/useBiometricAuth.ts` (new)
  **Action:** After successful password login, offer to enable biometric. On subsequent launches, attempt biometric → unlock SecureStorage token → skip password. Fallback to password after 3 failures.

### Phase 5 — SQLite Offline Storage

- [ ] Task 18: Install and verify SQLite plugin
  **Action:** `npm install @capacitor-community/sqlite`. Before building the StorageAdapter, verify: (1) plugin supports Capacitor 6.x (check package.json peer deps), (2) no open critical bugs on GitHub issues, (3) test basic CRUD on both iOS simulator and Android emulator. If plugin is unmaintained or broken, fallback to `@nicepay/capacitor-sqlite` or raw WebSQL.

- [ ] Task 19: Create StorageAdapter abstraction
  **File:** `frontend/src/services/offlineStorage.ts` (new)
  **Action:** Interface with `enqueue()`, `replay()`, `getSize()`, `clear()`. Two implementations: `IndexedDbAdapter` (existing offlineQueue.ts logic) and `SqliteAdapter` (new). Platform detection selects at runtime.

- [ ] Task 20: Migrate offlineQueue.ts to use StorageAdapter
  **File:** `frontend/src/services/offlineQueue.ts`
  **Action:** Refactor to delegate to the StorageAdapter. Existing behavior unchanged on web. SQLite path on native. **Both paths must be tested:** web path verified by existing Playwright tests (no regression), native SQLite path verified manually on physical device (Task 26) — enqueue hold while airplane mode, verify SQLite contains the record, disable airplane mode, verify replay succeeds.

### Phase 6 — App Store Submission

- [ ] Task 21: Apple Privacy manifest
  **File:** `ios/App/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`
  **Action:** Declare data collection practices: authentication tokens, device tokens, usage analytics (none currently). Required since May 2024.

- [ ] Task 22: App Store screenshots and metadata
  **Action:** Capture screenshots on iPhone 15 Pro and iPad Pro simulators. Write App Store description, keywords, support URL. Include demo login credentials in review notes. **Apple Developer Program:** Standard program ($99/year) is sufficient for App Store distribution. Enterprise program ($299/year) only needed if hospital IT requires in-house MDM distribution without App Store. Start with standard — TestFlight supports up to 10,000 beta testers.

- [ ] Task 23: Google Play Store listing
  **Action:** Generate Play Store screenshots, write listing description, configure Digital Asset Links for deep linking.

- [ ] Task 24: OTA update pipeline
  **Action:** Evaluate OTA options: Capgo (SaaS, free tier 1,000 devices), `@capawesome/capacitor-live-update` (self-hosted), or Ionic Appflow (enterprise). Choose based on cost and control. Configure auto-update check on app launch. Verify Apple and Google compliance (JS-only updates, no native code changes). For a single-app open-source project, Capgo free tier is likely sufficient initially.

### Phase 7 — Testing & Verification

- [ ] Task 25: Verify PWA still works unchanged
  **Action:** Run full Playwright suite (Vite + nginx) — must pass with zero regressions. The Capacitor changes must not break the web experience.

- [ ] Task 26: Manual testing on physical devices (Go/No-Go checklist)
  **Action:** Test on physical iPhone + physical Android device. Every item must pass:
  - [ ] Login with password succeeds
  - [ ] Bed search loads with shelter results
  - [ ] Hold a bed → countdown appears
  - [ ] Coordinator availability update reflects in outreach search
  - [ ] Background the app → send availability update from another device → push notification banner appears
  - [ ] Kill the app → send availability update → push notification banner appears
  - [ ] Tap push notification → app opens to correct screen
  - [ ] Airplane mode → hold a bed → "Hold queued" shown → disable airplane mode → hold replays
  - [ ] Verify SQLite persists hold queue after app kill (reopen in airplane mode, queue still has the hold)
  - [ ] Biometric unlock on subsequent launch (Face ID / Touch ID / fingerprint)
  - [ ] Deep link `fabt://search` opens bed search
  - [ ] Dark mode renders correctly
  - [ ] App size < 25MB on both platforms

- [ ] Task 27: Submit to TestFlight (iOS) and Internal Testing (Android)
  **Action:** First submission for beta testing. Gather feedback from a small group before public release.

### Merge and Release

- [ ] Task 29: Submit to Apple App Store and Google Play Store
- [ ] Task 30: Update documentation (README, FOR-DEVELOPERS, runbook)

Scope: app-wide theme, color identity, typography, shape, motion tokens.
File groups: `app/lib/app.dart`, `app/lib/core/theme/*.dart`, `app/test/core/theme/*.dart`.

docs(openspec): design-fidelity-ui-primitive-sync change — primitive sync proposal

The v0 design source frequently uses extended shadcn primitive APIs
(CommandDialog with title/description, newer Dialog variants) that
the project-side src/components/ui/ does not implement. Skeleton check
passes, then the next gate dies with a TypeScript build error like
"Property 'title' does not exist on type 'DialogProps'".

This is a contract gap between v0-export/components/ui/ and the
project's primitive layer — not a v0/agent/build bug. Right now the
framework treats them as independent, so any v0-side primitive
customization causes a guaranteed retry cycle.

Artifacts propose adding sync_ui_primitives() to v0_importer.py that
mirrors v0-export/components/ui/**.tsx into src/components/ui/,
overwrites on byte-difference, never deletes, with INFO logging per
sync. Specs cover: ui-primitive-sync semantics, design-fidelity gate
behaviour, v0-design-import CLI plumbing.

No implementation in this commit — artifacts only.

anchor_commit_observation.message:
fix(picker): keep selected card visible when card heights vary

The picker's vertical scroll math assumes a fixed `pageSize` cached
from the previous render, but the render itself greedily packs cards
into a fixed line budget where each card's height varies (Prompt row,
clampWarning, hotkeyConflict, hotkeyShadowsBuiltin, availability
status, Drift, Shadowing). When the next frame's cards are slightly
taller than the previous frame's, the packer fits one fewer card,
the state-layer scroll math is blind to the disagreement, and the
freshly-selected card lands outside the actual packed range. User-
visible symptom: pressing Down (or PgDn) past a card-height
boundary makes the selection marker disappear; the next press
appears to "skip" a card because the previously-selected card was
never rendered.

This change makes the picker's render self-correct. After the
greedy pack, if the selected card is outside the packed range, the
render computes a corrected scroll offset that anchors the
selection back into view, re-packs once, and propagates the
corrected offset back into picker state. The correction loop is
bounded at 3 iterations (with an early-break-when-unchanged guard)
so cases where the corrected window itself contains taller cards
still converge on the same frame. The fix covers Down, PgDn, Up,
PgUp, and Filter-mode arrows uniformly.

What's in:
- src/ui/picker-state.ts: add pure `clampScrollToFit(state,
  packedCount, visibleCount)` helper. Handles both the downward-
  overshoot case (selectedIndex past packed range) and the
  upward-overshoot case (selectedIndex before scrollOffset).
  Idempotent by construction; non-actionable when packedCount or
  visibleCount is zero.
- src/ui/picker.ts: split the greedy packer into a parameterized
  `packList(width, scrollOffset)`. Replace `renderList(width):
  string[]` with `renderList(width): { lines, renderedCards,
  correctedScrollOffset? }`. Apply the correction in a bounded
  loop (max 3 attempts, early break on unchanged offset). Outer
  `render(width)` reads `correctedScrollOffset` and updates state
  via `clampScrollToFit` before the next user keystroke.

Tighten layered construction: name uniqueness, phased prompt, archive

Real-world test against qwen2.5:14b on the Marshall Fire transcript
exposed two bugs: the duplicate-call detector only caught identical
consecutive calls (so add_resource("Claimant") with different args
slipped through), and an Ollama edge case returned an empty assistant
turn that crashed the loop. Added a `duplicate_name` check per primitive
kind and a tolerance for empty assistant content. Tightened the layered
system prompt with mandatory phase ordering (nouns → memberships →
operations → tasks → processes → triggers/rules → finalize), explicit
naming examples, and a guard against early finalize.

Also archives the openspec change and syncs the new layered-construction
spec into openspec/specs/.

refactor(sruth): move sruth/ → docs/sruth/ (the pre-v4 subtree)

Per the user's plan: `sruth/` (61MB legacy pre-v4 sub-project
tree) is moved to `docs/sruth/` where it joins the other
documented history (`docs/agents/`, `docs/dagster/`,
`docs/INTEGRATIONS_INDEX.md`, etc.).

The move uses `git mv` with rename detection; `.gitignore` was
updated to point at the new path. The `docs/sruth/oideachais/notebooks/**/
__marimo__/session/` exclusion pattern is preserved.

**Why this change:**

After the 2026-07-17 v7 flattening (commit `2026-07-17-v7-flatten-\ncianfhoghlaim-merge-bonneagar-rewrite-readme-license-v1`),\nthe `sruth/` subtree was retained as a separate legacy tree.
The decision was: `sruth/` would be deprecated but kept
in-tree for historical reference. Now that:

- The cianfhoghlaim core has stabilized (Mega-3 a/b/c all
  committed)
- The agent fleet has consolidated (15 agents in AGENT_REGISTRY)
- The web monorepo + integration runtimes are wired

…the sruth/ subtree is fully legacy and should live alongside
the other documented-history artifacts (`docs/CHOP_AND_CHANGE_GUIDE.md`,
`docs/FAMILY_HISTORY.md`, etc.) rather than at the repo root.

**Net changes:**

- 3139 renames: `sruth/<path>` → `docs/sruth/<path>`
- 4 .gitignore updates: `sruth/oideachais/...` → `docs/sruth/...`
- 1 sruth/oideachais/notebooks/__marimo__/session pattern updated

This is the move-only commit. The bulk cocoindex-flows sweep of\ndocs/sruth/ is deferred — the docs/ tree is documentation, not\nactive code, so the rename applies only to reference docs (which\nmostly correctly say 'cocoindex_flows' already — only 5–10\nreferences remained drifted in sruth/).

manual-test-only remaining, superseded by recent work, or never started.

memory-hook-optimization, fix-e2e-gate-timeout-masking, reduce-change-retry-waste,
orchestration-pause-resume, agent-page-discuss-button-with-voice,
session-context-analyzer, design-layer-separation (bridge.sh tests superseded by
v0-only-design-pipeline §7 removal), unified-web-service (12 AC validations,
30d stale).

Superseded (4): shadcn-ui-design-connector → v0-only-design-pipeline (v0 IS the
design source); design-compliance-gate → design-fidelity-gate from v0-only;
unified-web-server (no tasks) → unified-web-service; fix-iss-007-also-open
→ fix-iss-lifecycle-hardening already covers.

Abandoned (14): fix-e2e-infra-systematic, fix-supervisor-restart-merge-bypass,
sentinel-supervisor-redesign, llm-verdict-classifier, fix-context-window-metric,
merge-checkpoints, nis2-compliance-layer, interactive-triage,
docs-screenshot-pipeline, learnings-to-rules, unified-orchestration-logging,
visual-e2e-smoke-tests, isolation-backend, diagnostic-pipeline. All 0/N or 11/15
with no movement in 12-37 days.

Most archived with --skip-specs (delta sync would have polluted main specs with
phantom requirements for never-implemented features) and --no-validate (the
delta files themselves carry the recurring `## IN SCOPE` inside `## ADDED
Requirements` structural issue; main specs are the source of truth, deltas are
historical).

Active scope kept: add-client-boundary-gate (2d), v0-only-design-pipeline
(in flight), e2e-test-scaffolding/enforcement/smoke-functional-split (real
unit-test work), docs-rewrite-release (continuation planned).

anchor_commit_observation.message:
refactor: split specflow-run into core runtime + local CLI wiring (#98)

Extract the seven workflow commands (start, advance, suspend, resume,
status, update-field, get-field) from src/bin/specflow-run.ts into a new
src/core/ module. Each command now accepts RunArtifactStore,
ChangeArtifactStore, WorkspaceContext, and a pre-parsed
WorkflowDefinition through explicit per-command dependency objects and
returns Result<Ok, CoreRuntimeError> — no process.argv, no filesystem
discovery, no git, no process.exit inside core.

src/bin/specflow-run.ts shrinks to a thin wiring layer that parses argv,
discovers state-machine.json (project-local → dist → installed),
constructs LocalFs*ArtifactStore and LocalWorkspaceContext, invokes the
core function, and maps the Result to stdout / stderr / exit code. Every
stderr message is preserved byte-for-byte; CLI flags, exit codes, and
stdout JSON are unchanged.

Test layout:
- src/tests/core-*.test.ts (25 unit tests) exercises the runtime with
  in-memory stores and a fake WorkspaceContext.
- src/tests/core-error-wording.test.ts (17 tests) pins each
  CoreRuntimeError.kind message against a fixture to catch drift.
- src/tests/core-purity.test.ts (3 guardrails) forbids node:fs,
  node:child_process, node:path, node:os, node:process, process.*, and
  imports from src/bin/ inside src/core/.
- src/tests/specflow-run.test.ts trimmed 27 → 10 smoke tests
  (807 → 384 LOC) that cover argv parsing, workflow-JSON discovery, the
  not_in_git_repo JSON surface, one Result→stderr+exit mapping, a full
  happy-path integration run, and legacy on-disk run.json compatibility.

Issue: https://github.com/skr19930617/specflow/issues/98

* fix: allow workspace.yaml without engine: block when engines.yaml exists

When engines.yaml is present in the config dir, the engine: block in

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: look up engines.yaml from global config dir in multi-workspace setup

In production, each workspace has its own configDir under ~/.railyn/workspaces/<name>/
but engines.yaml lives at ~/.railyn/config/ (the global config dir).

The previous fix checked join(configDir, 'engines.yaml') which missed the global
location. Now both the presence check and loadEnginesConfig() fall back to
getDefaultConfigDir() so engines.yaml at ~/.railyn/config/ is correctly picked up
for any workspace.

* fix: don't inherit global engines.yaml when workspace.yaml has engine: block

When a workspace has engine: type: claude in workspace.yaml, it should only
expose that engine — not fall back to loading all engines from the global
engines.yaml. The global engines.yaml fallback now only applies when workspace.yaml
has no engine: block at all (pure multi-engine workspace).

This prevented spurious 'copilot Auto' from appearing in the model picker for
workspaces that only use claude via the legacy engine: config.
